newsitem.title: FRANCE: Arthuis says 1997 net tax cuts 25.5 bln Ffr.
newsitem.headline: Arthuis says 1997 net tax cuts 25.5 bln Ffr.

text.p: French Finance Minister Jean Arthuis said on Wednesday that the 1997 tax burden would fall by a net 25.5 billion francs.

Arthuis said that in addition to the 25 billion franc income tax cuts a series of tax incentives, introduced at the beginning of 1996 to boost consumer spending, would be worth 13.5 billion francs in 1997, taking total tax cuts to 38.5 billion francs.
Increases in other taxes, however, will partly offset these cuts leaving a net reduction of 25.5 billion, Arthuis said.

The CSG tax, a flat tax on most income, will raise seven billion francs while a 4.8 billion franc increase in tobacco taxes and a 1.2 billion franc rise in alcohol tax would take the total tax increases to 13 billion.
